Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. I'm opening a priority incident (OPS-1329) and looping in reliability + CS.

Immediate plan (10–30m):
- Run a short mitigation: reduce batch size on Veridian routing to limit HOL blocking and cap batch lane concurrency to 4.
- Tighten KV cache TTLs and eviction aggressiveness for tenant namespace to reduce cache thrash.
- If needed, pin to the lower-latency model variant for 30 minutes while we stabilize.

Can you confirm you give us permission to apply those mitigations on your production stack? We will coordinate the exact window and rollback plan.

I'll schedule a 10:30 call and send a Zoom link.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ops@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-22T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High p99 latency and 5xx spike — mitigation steps

Marissa / team — quick ops notes (for the call and for the runbook):

Observations from logs (veridian_incident_snippet):
- Hot-key skew: ~12% of requests target a small set of prefix keys (session/tenant buckets).
- High prefetched KV churn: large values + long prefetch TTLs causing eviction storms on >1 GPUs.

Short-term commands (apply now, rollback with previous config):
1) Set kv.namespace.veridian.eviction_policy = "aggressive-ttl" (TTL: 30s, priority: tenant_high). See kv-policy-diff.patch.
2) Per-route cap: route.veridian.batch_lane.max_concurrency = 4
3) batch.global.default_max_tokens = 256 (reduce batching window)
4) Disable async background prefetch for tenant namespace: kv.prefetch.enabled=false

Reasoning: capping concurrency and shrinking batch windows reduces HOL blocking; aggressive TTL prevents large keys from thrashing LRU.

I'll apply 1–2 as a canary on 2 nodes first, monitor p99 and 5xx for 10m, then roll to full pool.

(attachment: kv-policy-diff.patch)
—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-mitigation update: Veridian incident and next steps

Team / Grace — final update on the Veridian incident.

Timeline & outcome:
- 2028-08-22 09:50 PDT: Canary changes applied to 2 nodes (kv TTL + batch cap).
- 09:55 PDT: p99 dropped from ~1.8s to ~0.28s on canary; 5xx rate fell to ~0.1%.
- 10:10 PDT: Rollout to full pool completed. By 10:20 p99 stabilized around 220ms and 5xx <0.05%.

Post-mortem (short):
- Root cause: tenant-level KV churn + long prefetch TTLs produced eviction storms under a 3x traffic ramp; large values caused hot partitions and HOL blocking in batching lanes.
- Immediate mitigations: aggressive TTL for tenant namespace, per-route batch_lane.max_concurrency cap, reduced global batching window, disabled background prefetch for tenant.
- Short-term impact: customer sessions recovered; no data loss.

Next steps (RCA + stable fix):
1) Engineering: implement adaptive TTL heuristics and per-tenant prefetch budgets (ETA: 3 weeks).
2) Product: add tenant hotkey protection knobs in the Console UI (ETA: 4 weeks).
3) CS/Sales: Marissa to propose a service credit/discount; recommend 15% credit for the impacted billing period unless leadership prefers an alternate concession.
4) Ops: finalize a runbook (OPS-1329) and schedule a tabletop for similar traffic ramps.

Attachments: post-mortem-draft.md (draft RCA), kv-policy-diff.patch (applied canary diff).

Ben — can you confirm numbers below so Marissa can draft the customer note?

—Ben
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
